description.en-US:
numpwd keeps a list of key names and turns a key name plus a password into a six-digit code. The code is exactly what this shell pipeline prints when you type the same password at its prompt: 
openssl passwd -6 -salt KEYNAME | tr -dc '[0-9]' | head -c6
Below the code the app shows the whole digit string (the pipeline without head -c6), which "Copy all" copies. So you can always recompute them on any computer with OpenSSL, without the app.
  • Only key names are stored. The password is never saved, logged, offered to autofill or learned by the keyboard.
  • The password field shows only dots, from the first keystroke, even with the system "Show passwords" setting on.
  • The password and result dialogs block screenshots and screen recording.
  • Copy buttons for the code and the whole string; the clipboard is cleared after 30 seconds and the result closes after a minute.
  • Tested against hundreds of vectors generated by the openssl binary, including UTF-8 names, names longer than 16 bytes, "$" and "rounds=N$" in names, and long passwords.
  • No permissions, no network.
Note: tr keeps '[' and ']' too, because the brackets are part of its character set, so a key name that contains brackets yields them in the output as well, and they count towards the six characters of the code. In the rare case that the pipeline prints fewer than six characters, the app shows what there is, as head -c6 does. numpwd is a fork of FreeOTP (Apache License 2.0).
